prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. One finished replacement portrait for ISAKA Tsuyoshi's chosen illustrated avatar, for the ARC Daily Card Cabinet. Input1 governs character identity: dark tousled hair, gentle thoughtful expression, charcoal hoodie silhouette, cup motif. It is a fictional account avatar, NOT a verified human photo. Input2 is the EDITOR-ACCEPTED new 1950s pulp/cyberpunk art direction: match its hand-inked, textured printed treatment, enthusiastic rocket-age machinery, enormous graphics-card hardware and colorful square ARC screens. Do not copy the woman's face, glasses, scarf, pose or costume.

Transform the anime cup-holder into a naturally proportioned ADULT MALE retro-futuristic space engineer from a beautifully painted 1950s American science-fiction comic. Short tousled black hair, normal-sized dark eyes, adult cheekbones and jaw, clean-shaven face, warm subtle smile. Face rendered with authentic mid-century gouache planes, ink crosshatching and fine print halftone, exactly the same medium as neck, hands and hardware. NO anime, manga, chibi, giant eyes, baby face, feminine makeup, photographic skin or photo-head collage.

Make the facial cybernetics indispensable and physically connected: bulky chrome radio headset with copper coils, riveted temple mounts, a compact green square CRT eyepiece covering ONE eye, wired cheek communications module and articulated jaw/neck collar. Hair stays visible above forehead; other eye, nose and smile remain readable. Several thick cables visibly route from headgear to the giant GPU rig. Everything fits head anatomy and is drawn together. Dark navy and teal work suit with cream pressure-collar panels and restrained scarlet utility accents; no scarf, hood down. Industrial compute pack with TWO ludicrously oversized TRIPLE-FAN graphics cards mounted diagonally behind shoulders, each nearly torso-sized, clearly visible fan blades, exposed circuit-board edges, deep aluminum heat sinks, fat copper coolant tubes, red enamel radiator fins, glowing vacuum tubes and analog lamps. GPUs must unmistakably look like graphics cards, not medieval shoulder armor. Distinct visible ARC-square tile displays on optics, forearm and chest. One gloved hand carries a compact SEALED brushed-steel coffee flask, echoing the avatar's mug, other hand adjusts a large rotary dial on a chest computer.

Atmospheric orbital engine room with curved observatory window, small distant ringed planet and square ARC-puzzle star patterns. He stands in a breathable interior. Warm mustard/cream key light and turquoise shadows, dark navy printed starfield. Strong confident black brush outlines, fine halftone, painted gouache shading, slightly offset four-color print registration and warm paper grain. Bright, sincere, lightly ridiculous mid-century space-adventure optimism. Rich polished illustration, no glossy 3D/photoreal render.

Portrait5:7, ideally1500x2100. Head-to-waist heroic portrait, face at upper third, complete headgear and oversized GPU silhouette in frame, keep essential props in upper70%; lower25% calmer deep-navy continuation for later stats. Full bleed. NO words, numbers, letters, names, labels, logos, watermark, comic title, caption boxes, speech balloons, card frame or border. ONE character only.

review: Retained first corrected illustration. Editor then requested more equipment variety; twin GPU setup and same pose repeat the prior heroine too closely. Replaced by the separate field-radio composition.
commissionAuthority: Boss requested retro-futuristic replacements for anime avatars, integrated face hardware, no scarves and varied equipment on 30 October 2026.
archiveNote: Exact native PNG and earlier originals retained. Fictional character adaptations are not verified human likenesses.
